chronology.event: An earlier wooden church may have stood on the site.
The standing Romanesque stone church was probably built and consecrated.
A sacristy was built on the north side of the chancel.
The municipality acquired the formerly privately owned church.
The west wall and porch were removed, the nave was extended and the interior was extensively altered under Halfdan Berle.

interpretationLimits: Year 1250 is approximate and not an exact documented construction or consecration date.
The possible earlier wooden church is a hypothesis and is not used as the canonical year.
The 1904 work is a major extension of a surviving medieval church, not a complete replacement building.
The canonical point represents the church building, not the full churchyard or Skjønhaug centre.
Trøgstad bygdemuseum, the chapel and the rectory are separate components.
Services, funerals and cemetery use take priority over gameplay.
